$comment: Content for Spectrum (node g32, ages 15-18, Chapter 5): NEW v2 build to GDD 32 (mechanic-embodying), the
identity / orientation / respect node (Thread D · Relationships). "People differ in who they are and who
they love, and every person deserves dignity, respect and safety: that part isn't a debate." 84 researched,
India-grounded, never-explicit scenarios across the-spectrum → myths-and-respect → dignity-for-all → being-you
→ stand-against-bullying → support-and-rights, each encoded as one of the shared v2 play actions (reflect /
branch / strike-rewrite / sort / role-play / match / spot): no binary "tap the right card". Lead: strike-
rewrite (bust the myth kindly), branch (your move), reflect. Built on ONE non-negotiable: respect is a value,
not a debate. Teaches understanding and busts harmful myths WITHOUT disparaging anyone's family or beliefs
separates honest belief-differences (respected) from the dignity floor (always upheld). Supports anyone
questioning, NO pressure to label, complete confidentiality; never outs or infers anyone; sharing is always
the person's own choice. India: consensual same-sex relations decriminalised (2018), NALSA recognised
transgender persons, dignity & equality are constitutional values; framed around settled values, not contested
policy. Routes distress / family-conflict to a trusted adult / counsellor, Tele-MANAS 14416,
Childline 1098. Builds on g7 & g25; links g27 & g31. gameId "spectrum".
title: Spectrum
greet: Hey, I’m Lensy. 🌈 People differ in who they are and who they love, and every person deserves dignity, respect and safety. That isn’t a debate. Let’s explore.

badge.title: Spectrum 🌈
badge.blurb: You understand the spectrum, you can bust harmful myths kindly without disparaging anyone, and you stand for dignity, respect and safety for every person. 🫶

helpLine: Whoever you are and whoever you love, you deserve dignity, respect and safety. Need support? Call Tele-MANAS 14416 or Childline 1098.
reassure: Who you are and who you love is yours, no pressure to label. Struggling or facing conflict at home? Call Tele-MANAS 14416 or Childline 1098. 🫶

scenarios.hook: Lensy: people differ in who they are and who they love, and that's just part of being human. Sit with that.
scenarios.affirm: Human diversity in identity and love is natural and as old as humanity itself.
scenarios.relearn: People vary in who they are and who they love; that's natural human diversity.

scenarios.hook: Match the term to its plain meaning.

pairs.right: Your own sense of your gender
How you treat everyone, no exceptions
What you share is your own choice

scenarios.relearn: Orientation is who you're drawn to; gender identity is your own sense of self; an ally supports dignity.

scenarios.hook: Sort: accurate, respectful language, or not?

items.text: Using the words people use for themselves

scenarios.relearn: Use the words people use for themselves; ask respectfully if unsure.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: this diversity isn't new or foreign, it spans cultures and history, including India's own. Did you know that?
scenarios.affirm: India has its own long-acknowledged traditions of diversity; this is part of human history everywhere.
scenarios.relearn: Diversity in identity spans cultures and history, including India's own traditions.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a fact about the spectrum, or a misunderstanding?

items.text: It's existed across all of history
It's part of India's own history

scenarios.relearn: Natural variation across history is fact; 'all the same', 'new fad' or 'foreign import' are misunderstandings.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: understanding isn't about labelling anyone, it's just replacing rumour with calm facts. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Calm, accurate understanding, with no pressure to label anyone, is the whole aim here.
scenarios.relearn: Understanding replaces rumour with facts; it never means labelling anyone.

scenarios.hook: "There are only two ways to be, and everyone fits neatly."

myth.un: Everyone fits neatly into two fixed boxes.
myth.re: Human identity and attraction vary more than two neat boxes allow.
myth.why: Real people are more varied than the stereotype.

scenarios.relearn: Human identity varies more than two neat boxes; that's normal.

scenarios.hook: Match the idea to the plain truth.

pairs.right: It's part of India's own history

scenarios.relearn: Orientation and identity vary, dignity is for everyone, and this diversity is old and Indian too.

scenarios.hook: Sort: respectful curiosity, or crossing a line?
scenarios.relearn: Learning, listening and gentle asking are respectful; demanding, prying and spreading guesses cross a line.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you can understand and respect people without needing to know or decide anything about anyone. See that?
scenarios.affirm: Respect doesn't require knowing anyone's private identity, it's simply how you treat people.
scenarios.relearn: You can respect everyone without needing to know anything private about them.

scenarios.hook: "Talking about this 'creates' more of it."

myth.un: Talking about diversity 'creates' or spreads it.
myth.re: Understanding doesn't create anything; it just replaces fear with facts.
myth.why: People are who they are; information doesn't change that.

scenarios.relearn: Understanding diversity doesn't create it; it replaces fear with facts.

scenarios.hook: Sort: part of natural human diversity, or a harmful label?
scenarios.relearn: Variation is natural; 'illness', 'to fix' or 'not natural' are harmful, false labels.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: which feels truest, people are varied and that's normal, or everyone must be the same?
scenarios.affirm: Variety is the human norm; expecting everyone to be identical is the myth.
scenarios.relearn: Human variety is normal; expecting everyone to be the same is the myth.

scenarios.hook: Match the respectful move to the moment.

pairs.right: Ask kindly or look it up

scenarios.relearn: Listen, ask kindly, don't pry, decline slurs and respect people even when unsure. That's respect in practice.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: calm, accurate understanding is the foundation for everything else here. Ready to build on it?
scenarios.affirm: With calm understanding in place, respect and dignity follow naturally.
scenarios.relearn: Calm, accurate understanding is the foundation for respect and dignity.

scenarios.hook: "It's just a choice people make."

myth.un: Orientation or identity is just a choice.
myth.re: It isn't a choice; it's part of who someone naturally is.
myth.why: People don't choose who they're drawn to or their sense of self.

scenarios.relearn: Orientation and identity aren't a choice; they're part of who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "It's just a phase they'll grow out of."

myth.un: It's just a phase they'll grow out of.
myth.re: For many it's a lasting part of who they are; it's not yours to time or dismiss.
myth.why: Dismissing it as 'a phase' can be hurtful and isn't for others to decide.

scenarios.relearn: It's not 'just a phase' for others to dismiss; it's part of who they are.

scenarios.hook: "It's a mental illness that needs curing."

myth.un: It's a mental illness that needs curing.
myth.re: It is not a mental illness; health bodies removed it from illness classifications long ago.
myth.why: Calling it an illness is false and causes real harm.

scenarios.relearn: It is not a mental illness; that idea is false and harmful.

scenarios.hook: "It's contagious, being around it spreads it."

myth.un: It's contagious, being around it spreads it.
myth.re: It isn't contagious; people are who they are, and understanding changes nothing about that.
myth.why: Identity isn't caught from others.

scenarios.relearn: Identity isn't contagious; you can't 'catch' who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "It's a foreign, Western import."

myth.un: It's a foreign, Western import.
myth.re: It exists across cultures and history, including India's own long traditions.
myth.why: This diversity is part of human history everywhere, not imported.

scenarios.relearn: It's not a foreign import; it spans cultures and India's own history.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: people can hold different personal beliefs AND still agree everyone deserves safety. Both at once?
scenarios.affirm: Honest differences of belief and a shared floor of dignity for all can coexist, that's the whole approach.
scenarios.relearn: People can differ in belief and still uphold dignity and safety for all.

scenarios.hook: "If you disagree with someone's life, you don't have to be kind to them."

myth.un: Disagreeing means you don't owe someone kindness or safety.
myth.re: You don't have to agree with everyone to treat everyone with dignity and keep them safe.
myth.why: Dignity and safety aren't conditional on agreement.

scenarios.relearn: You can disagree and still owe everyone dignity and safety.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a harmful myth, or an understanding that replaces it?

items.text: "It's a phase to grow out of"

scenarios.relearn: 'Choice', 'illness' and 'phase' are myths; 'part of who someone is' and 'natural variation' are the truth.

scenarios.hook: Sort: respects a person, or disparages them?

items.text: Shaming a person for who they are
Using the words people use for themselves
Throwing a slur to win a point

scenarios.relearn: Correcting kindly, upholding safety and using people's own words respects them; mocking, shaming and slurs disparage.

scenarios.hook: "Caring about this means attacking people's traditions."

myth.un: Standing for dignity means attacking people's traditions.
myth.re: It means upholding a floor of respect and safety for everyone, without disparaging anyone.
myth.why: Dignity for all and respect for people's backgrounds can both be held.

scenarios.relearn: Standing for dignity upholds safety for all without attacking anyone's traditions.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: the one thing that isn't up for debate is that everyone deserves to be safe. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Whatever anyone believes, everyone's safety and dignity is the non-negotiable floor.
scenarios.relearn: Everyone's dignity and safety is the one thing not up for debate.

scenarios.hook: "People like that don't really deserve respect."

myth.un: 'People like that' don't deserve respect.
myth.re: Every single person deserves dignity, respect and safety, no exceptions.
myth.why: There is no group outside the floor of human dignity.

scenarios.relearn: Every person deserves dignity, respect and safety, no exceptions.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a settled fact, or a discredited claim?
scenarios.relearn: 'Not an illness', 'occurs across history' and 'not catchable' are settled; 'curable', 'modern' and 'spreads' are discredited.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: busting a myth kindly, without putting anyone down, is a real skill. Want to practise it?
scenarios.affirm: Correcting a falsehood while respecting the person is exactly the skill this game builds.
scenarios.relearn: You can correct a myth kindly, without putting anyone down.

scenarios.hook: "Understanding this is dangerous for young people."

myth.un: Understanding diversity is dangerous for young people.
myth.re: Accurate understanding reduces fear, bullying and harm; misinformation is what's dangerous.
myth.why: Knowledge and respect keep young people safer, not less safe.

scenarios.relearn: Accurate understanding reduces harm; misinformation is the real danger.

scenarios.hook: Friends start mocking someone with slurs about their identity.

options.text: Don't join; calmly say it's not okay, or step away and support the person
options.consequence: You uphold their dignity safely.

options.text: Laugh along to fit in
options.consequence: Laughing fuels it; calmly declining or supporting the person is the dignified move.

scenarios.debrief: You don't have to make a scene; not joining and quietly supporting counts.
scenarios.relearn: Don't join slurs; calmly decline or support the person.

scenarios.hook: Someone is being left out because of who they are.

options.text: Include them, simply and warmly
options.consequence: They feel they belong.

options.text: Go along with the exclusion
options.consequence: A simple, warm inclusion is dignity in action.

scenarios.debrief: Quiet inclusion is one of the most powerful forms of respect.
scenarios.relearn: Including someone warmly is everyday dignity in action.

scenarios.hook: You feel unsure about these topics, but someone near you is bullied for their identity.

options.text: You don't have to agree on everything to keep them safe, so help
options.consequence: You uphold the dignity floor whatever your own views.

options.text: Stay out of it because you're unsure
options.consequence: Safety isn't conditional on agreeing; keep them safe anyway.

scenarios.debrief: Dignity and safety don't depend on agreeing about everything.
scenarios.relearn: You can keep someone safe while working out your own views.

scenarios.hook: You want to gently shut down a slur without a big confrontation.

yourLine.text: "Let's not use that word, it's not okay."
Say nothing and let it stand

scenarios.relearn: A calm 'let's not use that word' upholds dignity without drama.

scenarios.hook: A friend is hurt by something said about them. Support them.

yourLine.text: "That was wrong of them. You deserve to be treated with respect."
"Just ignore it."

scenarios.relearn: Affirming someone's right to respect helps after they're hurt.

scenarios.hook: Spot the 2 moves that put the person at risk, not the safe ally moves.

scene.text: Sitting with someone who's excluded
A dramatic scene that turns the crowd on them
Calmly declining to join mockery
Posting 'I'm defending them' so all now know who
Quietly telling a teacher they need help

scenarios.why: A dramatic scene and an exposing post can endanger them; quiet support, declining and an adult are safe.
scenarios.relearn: Quiet, steady allyship, sitting with someone, declining mockery, is the safe kind.

scenarios.hook: You're tempted to 'out' someone you think might be different, as gossip.

options.text: Never, someone's private identity is theirs alone to share
options.consequence: You protect their safety and privacy.

options.text: Mention it to others
options.consequence: Outing someone can endanger them; it's never yours to share.

scenarios.debrief: Whether, when and to whom anyone shares anything is only ever their own choice.
scenarios.relearn: Never out anyone; a person's identity is theirs alone to share.

scenarios.hook: A classmate uses the right respectful words and others laugh at them for it.

options.text: Back them up; respectful language is the normal, decent default
options.consequence: You make respect the norm.

options.text: Laugh with the others
options.consequence: Respectful language is just decency; back the person using it.

scenarios.debrief: Treating respect as normal, not mockable, shifts the whole group.
scenarios.relearn: Back people who use respectful language; it's just decency.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: the 'win' here is always a person treated with dignity. Feel good about that goal?
scenarios.affirm: A person treated with dignity is the only scoreboard that matters here.
scenarios.relearn: The goal is always a person treated with dignity.

scenarios.hook: Sort each move: does it uphold dignity, or undermine it?
scenarios.relearn: Inclusion, privacy and support uphold dignity; slurs, gossip and outing undermine it.

scenarios.hook: Online, people are piling abuse on someone for their identity.

options.text: Don't add to it; report it and check the person is okay
options.consequence: You reduce harm and offer support.

options.text: Join in or share it on
options.consequence: Don't pile on; report it and support the person instead.

scenarios.debrief: Online, not piling on and reporting is the safe, decent move.
scenarios.relearn: For online identity abuse: don't pile on, report it, support the person.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: India's own constitution holds dignity and equality for all. Does that feel like solid ground to stand on?
scenarios.affirm: Dignity and equality for all are settled constitutional values, firm ground for respect.
scenarios.relearn: Dignity and equality for all are constitutional values in India.

scenarios.hook: You want to set a respectful tone in your friend group.

yourLine.text: "Whoever someone is, we treat them with respect here."
Leave it unspoken

scenarios.relearn: Naming 'we treat everyone with respect' sets the group's tone.

scenarios.hook: A friend just shared about themselves. Spot the 2 responses that disrespect them.

scene.text: "Thanks for telling me, I trust you too."
Acting shocked or making it weird
Treating them exactly the same
Telling friends 'guess what they said'
"I'm here whenever you want to talk."

scenarios.why: Making it weird and gossiping break trust; warmth, sameness and an open door are respect.
scenarios.relearn: Meet someone sharing with warmth and unchanged respect; keep it confidential.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you can be a steady, quiet ally without drama or risk to anyone. Reassuring?
scenarios.affirm: Steady, low-key allyship is both safe and genuinely powerful.
scenarios.relearn: You can be a steady, quiet ally without drama or risk.

scenarios.hook: Someone asks you to take a 'side' in mocking a group.

options.text: Decline; you can respect people without taking sides against any of them
options.consequence: You keep the dignity floor for everyone.

options.text: Pick the mocking side to fit in
options.consequence: You can opt out of mockery entirely and respect everyone.

scenarios.debrief: Respecting everyone isn't 'a side'; it's the floor under all of us.
scenarios.relearn: You can refuse to mock anyone and respect everyone.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: if you're ever unsure about your own feelings or identity, that's completely okay. Hear that?
scenarios.affirm: Being unsure is normal and fine; there's no timeline and no pressure here.
scenarios.relearn: It's completely okay to be unsure about yourself; there's no rush.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: there's no need to label yourself or decide anything to be okay. Does that take off some pressure?
scenarios.affirm: You don't owe anyone a label or a decision; you're okay exactly as you are.
scenarios.relearn: You don't need to label yourself or decide anything to be okay.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: whoever you are, you are not broken, and you are not alone. Let that land.
scenarios.affirm: You're not broken and you're never alone; many people understand and care.
scenarios.relearn: Whoever you are, you're not broken and not alone.

scenarios.hook: You're questioning things about yourself and wondering if you must tell people.

options.text: Remember: whether, when and who you tell is entirely your choice
options.consequence: You keep control of your own story.

options.text: Feel you must announce it to everyone now
options.consequence: There's no must; sharing is your choice, in your time, with people you trust.

scenarios.debrief: Your story is yours; you never have to share before you're ready, or at all.
scenarios.relearn: Whether, when and who you tell is entirely your own choice.

scenarios.hook: You're feeling low or confused and don't know who's safe to talk to.

options.text: Reach a trusted adult/counsellor or a confidential line (Tele-MANAS 14416)
options.consequence: You find real, caring support.

options.text: Keep it all inside
options.consequence: You don't have to carry it alone; trusted support and confidential lines exist.

scenarios.debrief: Confidential, caring support is there whenever you need it.
scenarios.relearn: If you're struggling, a trusted adult or Tele-MANAS 14416 can help.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: figuring yourself out is a journey, not a test with a deadline. Comforting?
scenarios.affirm: Self-understanding unfolds at its own pace; there's no deadline and no wrong way.
scenarios.relearn: Understanding yourself is a journey, not a deadline or a test.

scenarios.hook: A friend quietly confides they're questioning things about themselves.

yourLine.text: "Thank you for trusting me. There's no rush, and I'm here for you."
"So what are you then?"

scenarios.relearn: Meet a confiding friend with 'no rush, I'm here', never with pressure to define it.

scenarios.hook: A friend who confided is scared about who else might find out.

yourLine.text: "This stays with me. It's yours to share, only if and when you want."
"People will probably guess anyway."

scenarios.relearn: Promise and keep confidentiality; their story is theirs to share.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you deserve support and safety no matter what you're working out about yourself. Believe it?
scenarios.affirm: Support and safety are yours unconditionally, whatever you're figuring out.
scenarios.relearn: You deserve support and safety, whatever you're working out.

scenarios.hook: Someone pressures you to 'pick a label' or 'prove' something about yourself.

options.text: You owe no one a label or proof; take your own time
options.consequence: You keep your autonomy and peace.

options.text: Force an answer to satisfy them
options.consequence: You owe no one a label or proof; your pace is yours.

scenarios.debrief: No one is entitled to define you or rush you.
scenarios.relearn: You owe no one a label or proof; take your own time.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: many people have walked this path and are living happy, full lives. Hopeful?
scenarios.affirm: So many people understand this and go on to live happy, full lives; you can too.
scenarios.relearn: Many have walked this path to happy, full lives; you're not alone.

scenarios.hook: Family tension is rising around these topics and it's weighing on you.

options.text: Reach careful, confidential support to help you through it
options.consequence: You get help carrying a hard situation.

options.text: Bottle it up alone
options.consequence: Family tension is heavy; confidential support (Tele-MANAS 14416) can help.

scenarios.debrief: You don't have to navigate family tension alone; careful support exists.
scenarios.relearn: For family tension, reach confidential support like Tele-MANAS 14416 or a counsellor.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: your safety comes first, always, including deciding what's safe to share and when. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Your safety leads every decision about sharing; that judgement is yours.
scenarios.relearn: Your safety comes first, including what and when you share.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: whatever you discover about yourself, you are worthy of love and respect. Hold onto that?
scenarios.affirm: Your worth, your right to love and respect, never depends on any of this.
scenarios.relearn: Whoever you are, you are worthy of love and respect.

scenarios.hook: You witness identity-based bullying that could turn unsafe.

options.text: Don't confront danger alone; support the person and get an adult
options.consequence: You help safely and bring real backup.

options.text: Jump into a risky confrontation
options.consequence: For unsafe situations, support the person and get an adult, don't confront danger alone.

scenarios.debrief: Safe upstanding, support plus an adult, applies to identity-based bullying too.
scenarios.relearn: For identity bullying that could turn unsafe: support the person and get an adult.

scenarios.hook: A slur is being thrown around as a 'joke' in your group.

options.text: Name that it's not a joke, calmly
options.consequence: You stop normalising the slur.

options.text: Let it slide as banter
options.consequence: Slurs-as-jokes still harm; calmly naming it helps.

scenarios.debrief: 'Just a joke' slurs still cause harm; calmly naming it matters.
scenarios.relearn: Identity slurs aren't 'just jokes'; calmly name that they're not okay.

scenarios.hook: You want to support someone right after they were bullied for who they are.

yourLine.text: "That wasn't okay, and it's not your fault. I'm with you."
"Maybe don't stand out so much."

scenarios.relearn: Tell a bullied person: that wasn't okay, not your fault, I'm with you.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two red flags, the responses that aren't safe help.

scene.text: Quietly alerting a teacher
Filming it for laughs
Checking the person is okay after
Egging the bullies on for a reaction
Walking the person away from it

scenarios.why: Filming for laughs and egging the bullies on both make it worse, the two red flags.
scenarios.relearn: Alert an adult and check on the person; never film it or egg it on.

scenarios.hook: You realise you once joined in mocking someone's identity.

options.text: Own it, stop, and treat them with respect from now on
options.consequence: You change course and can even make amends.

options.text: Justify it to avoid feeling bad
options.consequence: Owning it and changing how you treat them is the better path.

scenarios.debrief: It's never too late to stop and choose respect.
scenarios.relearn: If you've mocked someone, own it, stop, and choose respect now.

scenarios.hook: Sort: helps a bullied person, or makes it worse?

items.text: Telling them to hide who they are

scenarios.relearn: Standing with, reporting and checking in help; 'hide yourself', gossip and filming make it worse.

scenarios.hook: A younger student is being teased about their identity and asks your help.

yourLine.text: "It's not your fault, and you deserve respect. Let's tell a teacher together."
"Just toughen up."

scenarios.relearn: Guide a teased junior: not your fault, you deserve respect, let's tell an adult.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: standing up for someone's dignity is a quiet kind of courage. Feel that?
scenarios.affirm: Choosing dignity for someone, even quietly, is real courage.
scenarios.relearn: Standing up for someone's dignity is a quiet, real courage.

scenarios.hook: You're scared that helping will make you a target too.

options.text: Use a safe move, tell an adult, support privately, you don't have to go it alone
options.consequence: You help without putting yourself at risk.

options.text: Do nothing out of fear
options.consequence: There are safe ways, telling an adult, quiet support, that don't expose you.

scenarios.debrief: You can help safely; safe upstanding doesn't require making yourself a target.
scenarios.relearn: Help safely, via an adult or quiet support; you needn't expose yourself.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two red flags, the things that make a group unsafe.

scene.text: Slurs are not tolerated
Everyone's treated with respect
'Banter' that targets who people are
People look out for each other
'Different' people get frozen out

scenarios.why: Identity-targeting 'banter' and freezing out the 'different' make a group unsafe, both red flags.
scenarios.relearn: Safe groups don't tolerate slurs, identity 'banter', or freeze-outs.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: a group where everyone's safe is better for everyone in it, not just some. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: A culture of respect protects and benefits everyone in the group.
scenarios.relearn: A group that's safe for everyone is better for all of its members.

scenarios.hook: "Bullying someone toughens them up."

myth.un: Bullying someone toughens them up.
myth.re: Bullying causes real harm and distress; it never 'helps' anyone.
myth.why: Identity-based bullying is linked to serious harm.

scenarios.relearn: Bullying harms; it never 'toughens' or helps anyone.

scenarios.hook: Match the need to where to turn (India).
scenarios.relearn: India support: Tele-MANAS 14416, Childline 1098, cybercrime helpline 1930, or a trusted adult.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: in India, dignity and equality for all are guaranteed by the Constitution. Solid to know?
scenarios.affirm: Dignity and equality for all are constitutional guarantees, firm ground to stand on.
scenarios.relearn: India's Constitution guarantees dignity and equality for all.

scenarios.hook: "Everyone different is breaking the law."

myth.un: Being who you are is against the law in India.
myth.re: Consensual same-sex relations between adults were decriminalised in 2018, and dignity is a constitutional right.
myth.why: The law protects dignity and privacy, not the opposite.

scenarios.relearn: Consensual same-sex relations between adults are decriminalised; dignity is a right.

scenarios.hook: "Transgender people have no recognition or rights."

myth.un: Transgender people have no recognition or rights in India.
myth.re: India's courts recognised transgender persons and their dignity and rights.
myth.why: Recognition and rights are settled, not absent.

scenarios.relearn: India recognises transgender persons and their dignity and rights.

scenarios.hook: A friend doesn't know any safe place to get support.

options.text: Point them to a trusted adult, counsellor or a confidential line
options.consequence: They find real, safe help.

options.text: Tell them there's nowhere to go
options.consequence: Trusted adults, counsellors and confidential lines (14416, 1098) are real options.

scenarios.debrief: Knowing the safe routes turns 'nowhere' into real support.
scenarios.relearn: Point a friend to a trusted adult, counsellor or confidential line.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: sharing anything about yourself is always your own choice, support never requires it. Reassuring?
scenarios.affirm: You can get support without disclosing anything; what you share is always your call.
scenarios.relearn: Getting support never requires disclosing anything; sharing is your choice.

scenarios.hook: Match the settled value to what it means.

pairs.right: There even if you share nothing

scenarios.relearn: Dignity, equality, privacy, safety and support all hold for every person.

scenarios.hook: You want to help make your school or group more respectful.

options.text: Model respect and back the dignity-for-all norm
options.consequence: You help build a safer culture for everyone.

options.text: Decide it's not your problem
options.consequence: Modelling respect and backing dignity-for-all helps everyone.

scenarios.debrief: Everyday modelling of respect is how a culture shifts.

options.text: Decide it's too risky and keep your distance

scenarios.relearn: Meet someone's sharing with warmth and unchanged respect.

yourLine.text: "Hey, come sit with us, there's space."

yourLine.text: "Let's not, na, everyone deserves respect."

scenarios.relearn: A gentle 'everyone deserves respect' holds the floor without a fight.

yourLine.text: "Hey, I was looking for you, let's go."
"What's wrong with you lot?!"

scenarios.relearn: A casual 'let's go' defuses and removes someone from harm without escalation.

yourLine.text: "Careful, that's not ours to tell."

scenarios.relearn: 'That's not ours to tell' stops an outing before it happens.

scenarios.relearn: You can disagree on things and still owe everyone dignity and safety.

myth.un: You have to agree with how someone lives to treat them with respect.
myth.re: You can disagree on things and still owe everyone dignity and safety.
myth.why: Respect is a basic floor for all people; it isn't a reward for agreeing with you.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: Quiet support, declining mockery and sitting with someone count fully.

myth.un: If you don't make a big public scene, you're not really standing up for anyone.
myth.re: Quiet support, declining mockery and sitting with someone count fully.
myth.why: Steady, low-key allyship is safe and real; courage doesn't need an audience.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: Someone's identity is theirs alone to share; never reveal, infer or imply it.

myth.un: If you've worked out something about a classmate, it's fine to tell friends.
myth.re: Someone's identity is theirs alone to share; never reveal, infer or imply it.
myth.why: Outing someone can put them at real risk; privacy is a safety feature, not gossip.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: Forwarding or commenting still piles on; report it and support the person.

myth.un: Sharing a mean post about someone is harmless, you didn't even write it.
myth.re: Forwarding or commenting still piles on; report it and support the person.
myth.why: Every share grows the harm and the audience; not engaging and reporting shrink it.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: You can support someone safely: sit with them, decline mockery, tell an adult.

myth.un: Standing up for someone always means putting yourself in danger.
myth.re: You can support someone safely: sit with them, decline mockery, tell an adult.
myth.why: For risky moments the safe move is support plus an adult, never solo confrontation.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: Differences of opinion are fine, but everyone's dignity and safety is settled.

myth.un: Whether some people deserve basic respect is a fair thing to debate.
myth.re: Differences of opinion are fine, but everyone's dignity and safety is settled.
myth.why: You can debate ideas without putting a person's basic worth up for a vote.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: Warmth and unchanged respect matter far more than finding perfect words.

myth.un: When a friend comes out to you, you have to say exactly the perfect thing.
myth.re: Warmth and unchanged respect matter far more than finding perfect words.
myth.why: A simple 'thanks for trusting me, nothing changes' is what truly reassures.

scenarios.hook: Strike the myth, write the truth.
scenarios.relearn: A simple 'come sit with us' is enough; warm, ordinary inclusion is the point.

myth.un: Including someone who's left out has to be a big, awkward gesture.
myth.re: A simple 'come sit with us' is enough; warm, ordinary inclusion is the point.
myth.why: Everyday, low-key inclusion is what actually makes someone feel they belong.

scenarios.hook: "They're only like this because of bad company."

myth.un: Someone is gay or trans because of the friends they keep.
myth.re: Who you're drawn to or your sense of self isn't set by your friends; it's part of who you are.
myth.why: Company shapes habits, not who someone fundamentally is.

scenarios.relearn: Friends don't make someone who they are; orientation and identity aren't 'caught' from company.

scenarios.hook: "With the right marriage it'll sort itself out."

myth.un: Marriage will 'fix' someone's orientation or identity.
myth.re: Marriage can't change who someone is; pushing it often causes deep harm to everyone involved.
myth.why: You can't marry away who a person naturally is.

scenarios.relearn: Marriage doesn't 'fix' anyone; orientation and identity aren't a problem to be solved.

scenarios.hook: "There were never people like this in our culture before."

myth.un: This diversity never existed in India before.
myth.re: India's own history and traditions have long acknowledged people who vary in this way.
myth.why: It's part of human history everywhere, India included, not a recent arrival.

scenarios.relearn: This isn't new to India; our own history has long acknowledged people who vary.

scenarios.hook: "It's just teenagers copying things they see online."

myth.un: Young people are just imitating what they see online.
myth.re: Seeing words for something doesn't create it; people have always varied, long before any screen.
myth.why: Having language for who you are isn't the same as being influenced into it.

scenarios.relearn: Words online don't create who someone is; people varied long before the internet.

scenarios.hook: "Counselling can change which gender someone feels they are."

myth.un: Therapy can change a person's gender identity.
myth.re: No therapy changes who someone is; trying to is discredited and can cause serious harm.
myth.why: Health bodies reject 'change' practices as harmful, not healing.

scenarios.relearn: No counselling changes who someone is; 'change' attempts are discredited and harmful.

scenarios.hook: "If we talk about it, more kids will turn out that way."

myth.un: Talking about diversity makes more young people gay or trans.
myth.re: Talking about it doesn't change who anyone is; it only replaces fear and silence with facts.
myth.why: Understanding can't make someone into something they aren't.

scenarios.relearn: Honest talk doesn't change who anyone is; it just replaces fear with facts.

scenarios.hook: "They're doing it for attention."

myth.un: People say they're LGBTQ just for attention.
myth.re: For most it's quietly part of who they are, often shared with real risk, not for show.
myth.why: Treating it as attention-seeking dismisses a real part of a person.

scenarios.relearn: It isn't done for attention; it's a real part of who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "You can tell what someone is from how they walk or dress."

myth.un: You can spot someone's orientation from how they look or move.
myth.re: How a person looks or moves tells you nothing reliable about who they're drawn to.
myth.why: Stereotypes about looks are guesses, and often wrong and hurtful.

scenarios.relearn: You can't read someone's orientation off their looks; that's just a stereotype.

scenarios.hook: "A boy who isn't tough must be gay."

myth.un: A gentle or non-sporty boy must be gay.
myth.re: Personality and interests aren't a sign of orientation; plenty of gentle boys are straight, and the reverse.
myth.why: Liking or not liking 'manly' things says nothing about who you love.

scenarios.relearn: A boy's interests or gentleness say nothing about his orientation.

scenarios.hook: "Two people of the same gender can't really love each other."

myth.un: Same-gender love isn't 'real' love.
myth.re: Love between two people of the same gender is as real and deep as any other love.
myth.why: The gender of the people doesn't make the feelings any less real.

scenarios.relearn: Same-gender love is real love, no less deep than any other.

scenarios.hook: "Being trans is just a fashion trend."

myth.un: Being trans is a passing trend.
myth.re: A trans person's sense of self is a deeply felt, lasting part of who they are, not a trend.
myth.why: Calling a real identity a 'trend' dismisses the person living it.

scenarios.relearn: Being trans isn't a trend; it's a deeply felt, lasting part of who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "They just haven't met the right person of the opposite sex."

myth.un: The right opposite-sex partner would change their orientation.
myth.re: Orientation isn't a gap waiting to be filled; who you're drawn to is part of who you are.
myth.why: No 'right person' rewrites who someone is naturally drawn to.

scenarios.relearn: There's no 'right person' that changes orientation; it's part of who you are.

scenarios.hook: "Respecting them means I have to agree with everything."

myth.un: Treating someone with dignity means agreeing with all their views.
myth.re: You can hold your own honest beliefs and still treat everyone with dignity and keep them safe.
myth.why: Respecting a person's safety isn't the same as agreeing with them.

scenarios.relearn: Dignity for all doesn't require agreement; safety isn't conditional on it.

scenarios.hook: "It's fine to laugh at them as long as it's a joke."

myth.un: Mocking someone's identity is okay if it's 'just a joke'.
myth.re: A slur dressed as a joke still wounds; humour that targets who someone is isn't harmless.
myth.why: 'Just joking' doesn't undo the hurt or make targeting okay.

scenarios.relearn: A joke that targets who someone is still hurts; 'just joking' doesn't excuse it.

scenarios.hook: "This is a disorder doctors should treat."

myth.un: It's a disorder that needs medical treatment.
myth.re: It is not a disorder; health bodies removed it from illness lists long ago, so there's nothing to treat.
myth.why: There's nothing broken to fix in who a person naturally is.

scenarios.relearn: It's not a disorder and needs no 'treatment'; that idea was dropped long ago.

scenarios.hook: "They'll grow out of it once they're older and serious."

myth.un: They'll outgrow it when they mature.
myth.re: For many it's a lasting part of who they are; it's not for others to time or wait out.
myth.why: Maturing changes a lot about a person, but not who they fundamentally are.

scenarios.relearn: It isn't something to 'grow out of'; it's a lasting part of who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "It's against nature."

myth.un: This kind of diversity is 'unnatural'.
myth.re: It's a natural, longstanding part of human variation, seen across cultures and history.
myth.why: What's longstanding and widespread across humans isn't outside nature.

scenarios.relearn: This variation is natural and longstanding, not 'against nature'.

scenarios.hook: "You're only allowed to respect people who are like you."

myth.un: Respect is only owed to people similar to you.
myth.re: Dignity is owed to everyone, including people whose lives look nothing like yours.
myth.why: The floor of human dignity has no 'people like me' exception.

scenarios.relearn: Respect isn't only for people like you; everyone is owed dignity.

scenarios.hook: "Correcting this myth means insulting whoever believes it."

myth.un: To bust a myth you have to put down the person who holds it.
myth.re: You can state the truth calmly and still treat the person who believed the myth with respect.
myth.why: Facts can be shared kindly; the person isn't the enemy.

scenarios.relearn: You can correct a myth and still respect the person who believed it.

scenarios.hook: "Keeping someone safe means I'm taking a side in a debate."

myth.un: Standing up for someone's safety is picking a political side.
myth.re: Everyone's safety and dignity isn't a debate position; it's the floor we all stand on.
myth.why: Safety being non-negotiable is settled ground, not a contest of opinions.

scenarios.relearn: Keeping someone safe isn't taking a side; safety is the floor, not a debate.

scenarios.hook: "If nobody talked about it, it would just disappear."

myth.un: Silence would make this diversity go away.
myth.re: Silence doesn't change who people are; it only leaves them more alone and unsafe.
myth.why: People exist whether or not anyone names it; silence just adds harm.

scenarios.relearn: Silence doesn't erase who people are; it only isolates them.

scenarios.hook: "You can pray or train it away if you try hard enough."

myth.un: Enough effort or prayer can change who someone is.
myth.re: Effort can't change who a person is; 'change' attempts are discredited and often cause real harm.
myth.why: Trying to change someone hurts them; it doesn't work.

scenarios.relearn: No amount of effort changes who someone is; 'change' attempts only harm.

scenarios.hook: "It must have been something the parents did wrong."

myth.un: A child is gay or trans because their parents made a mistake.
myth.re: It isn't caused by parenting or any 'mistake'; it's simply part of who the person is.
myth.why: Blaming parents adds guilt to a thing nobody did or could prevent.

scenarios.relearn: It isn't anyone's 'fault' or a parenting error; it's just who someone is.

scenarios.hook: "Calling it normal just encourages more of it."

myth.un: Saying this is normal makes more people 'become' it.
myth.re: Naming something as natural doesn't increase it; it just lets people who already vary feel safe.
myth.why: Acceptance changes how safe people feel, not who they are.

scenarios.relearn: Calling it normal doesn't 'encourage' it; it only helps people feel safe.

scenarios.hook: "They can hide it, so there's no real harm in mocking."

myth.un: Mockery is harmless because the person can just hide who they are.
myth.re: Forcing someone to hide and mocking them both cause real harm; neither is harmless.
myth.why: Asking a person to disappear to avoid your jokes isn't a kindness.

scenarios.relearn: Mockery isn't harmless; making someone hide who they are causes real harm.

scenarios.hook: "Real men and women don't question any of this."

myth.un: Anyone who questions their gender or whom they love is weak or confused.
myth.re: Working out who you are takes honesty and courage; it isn't weakness or confusion.
myth.why: Questioning is a normal, brave part of growing up for many people.

scenarios.relearn: Questioning who you are isn't weakness; it's an honest, normal part of life.

scenarios.hook: "It's a sickness you can pass to younger siblings."

myth.un: A younger sibling can 'catch' it from an older one.

scenarios.relearn: Human identity varies more than two neat boxes; that variety is normal.

scenarios.hook: "This is all brand new. It didn't exist before."

myth.un: This diversity is brand new and didn't exist before.
myth.re: It's longstanding across cultures and history, including India's own traditions.
myth.why: It's part of human life everywhere, far older than any 'trend'.

scenarios.relearn: This diversity isn't new; it's longstanding across history and India's own traditions.

scenarios.hook: "Understanding someone means you have to label them."

myth.un: Understanding someone means labelling or defining them.
myth.re: Understanding is just calm knowledge; it never means labelling or prying into anyone.
myth.why: You can know the facts and still let every person stay simply themselves.

scenarios.relearn: Understanding never means labelling anyone; it's just calm knowledge.

scenarios.hook: "You can't respect someone unless you know all about them."

myth.un: You must know everything about someone to respect them.
myth.re: Respect is just how you treat people; it never needs private details.
myth.why: Dignity doesn't depend on knowing anyone's private life.

scenarios.relearn: You can respect anyone without knowing anything private about them.

scenarios.hook: "Using their own word for themselves is just political correctness."

myth.un: Using the words people use for themselves is just 'political correctness'.
myth.re: It's simply basic respect: calling people what they ask to be called.
myth.why: Names and words for ourselves matter to everyone.

scenarios.relearn: Using people's own words is basic respect, not 'political correctness'.

scenarios.hook: "If everyone were normal, no one would be different."

myth.un: Being 'normal' means everyone is the same.
myth.re: Variety is the human norm; expecting everyone to be identical is the real myth.
myth.why: People have always differed. That's ordinary, not a flaw.

scenarios.relearn: Variety is normal; expecting everyone to be identical is the myth.

scenarios.hook: "Learning the facts about diversity makes more of it happen."

myth.un: Learning about diversity 'creates' or spreads it.
myth.re: Understanding doesn't create anything; it just replaces fear with facts.
myth.why: People are who they are; information doesn't change that.

scenarios.relearn: Understanding diversity doesn't create it; it replaces fear with facts.

scenarios.hook: A friend mentions they didn't know the right word and feels awkward. Reassure them.

yourLine.text: "No worries. Just ask people what they prefer. That's all respect needs."
"You should already know this stuff."

scenarios.relearn: It's fine not to know a word; just ask people what they prefer.

scenarios.hook: Someone's pressing you to guess a classmate's 'real' identity as gossip.

yourLine.text: "That's their business, not ours to guess or spread."
"Yeah, let's figure out what they are."

scenarios.relearn: It's not yours to guess or spread; let people's private business stay private.

scenarios.hook: A friend says 'people being different is just a modern fad'. Correct it kindly.

yourLine.text: "Actually it's really old, across history and India's own traditions too."
Just nod and say nothing

scenarios.relearn: Correct 'it's a fad' kindly: it's longstanding across history and India's own traditions.

scenarios.hook: Someone tells you they don't get why they 'have to' respect people unlike them.

yourLine.text: "You don't have to be like someone to treat them with respect."
"Yeah, why bother, honestly."

scenarios.relearn: You don't have to be like someone to treat them with respect.

scenarios.hook: A friend shares something about who they are, then looks nervous. Respond warmly.

yourLine.text: "Thanks for telling me. Nothing changes. We're good."
"Whoa, okay, that's a lot."

scenarios.relearn: Meet someone sharing with warmth and unchanged respect; nothing about your friendship changes.

scenarios.hook: Someone uses an outdated, insulting label for a group, not realising it stings.

yourLine.text: "That word's pretty outdated. People just use their own terms now."
Use the same word back

scenarios.relearn: Gently note an outdated label is dated; people use their own terms now.

scenarios.hook: A younger cousin asks you, plainly, what 'the spectrum' even means.

yourLine.text: "It just means people vary in who they are and who they love, and they always have."
"You're too young to ask that."

scenarios.relearn: The spectrum just means people vary in who they are and who they love.

scenarios.hook: A friend is curious but worried that asking questions is rude.

yourLine.text: "Kind questions are fine. Just ask gently and don't pry."
"Don't ask anything, ever."

scenarios.relearn: Kind, gentle questions are fine; the line is not prying or demanding.

scenarios.hook: You realise you don't know the right respectful word for something.

options.text: Ask kindly or look it up, then use the word people prefer
options.consequence: You get it right and show you care.

options.text: Guess and use whatever word comes to mind
options.consequence: A wrong word can sting; asking or looking it up is kinder and easy.

scenarios.debrief: Not knowing a word is fine; ask kindly or look it up and use people's own words.
scenarios.relearn: When unsure of a word, ask kindly or look it up; use the words people use for themselves.

scenarios.hook: A friend repeats 'this diversity stuff is a foreign import'.

options.text: Gently note it's part of India's own long history, not imported
options.consequence: You replace a rumour with a calm fact.

options.text: Agree to avoid an argument
options.consequence: It isn't imported. It's longstanding in India too; you can say so kindly.

scenarios.debrief: It isn't a foreign import; it's longstanding across cultures and India's own history.
scenarios.relearn: This diversity isn't a foreign import; it's part of India's own long history.

scenarios.hook: People want you to guess and label a quiet classmate.

options.text: Refuse: who anyone is, is theirs alone, not ours to label
options.consequence: You protect their privacy and dignity.

options.text: Join the guessing
options.consequence: It's not yours to guess or label; let people be simply themselves.

scenarios.debrief: Understanding never means labelling or guessing about any individual.
scenarios.relearn: Don't guess or label anyone; who someone is, is theirs alone.

scenarios.hook: A friend says 'I just don't get this, so I'll be rude about it.'

options.text: Remind them you can be unsure and still treat people with respect
options.consequence: You hold the respect floor while they learn.

options.text: Agree that not getting it excuses rudeness
options.consequence: Being unsure never excuses rudeness; you can learn and still be kind.

scenarios.debrief: You can be working things out and still treat everyone with respect.
scenarios.relearn: You can be unsure and still treat people with respect; confusion never excuses rudeness.

scenarios.hook: Someone shares a private guess about a third person's identity with you.

options.text: Don't repeat it: what's private about someone stays private
options.consequence: You keep them safe and respected.

options.text: Pass it along to others
options.consequence: Spreading guesses about people can harm them; let it stop with you.

scenarios.debrief: You can respect everyone without spreading anything private about them.
scenarios.relearn: Don't spread private guesses about people; what's private stays private.

scenarios.hook: A new student is unsure how they'll be treated in your group.

options.text: Be warm and ordinary: treat them with the same respect as anyone
options.consequence: They feel they simply belong.

options.text: Make a big curious deal of them
options.consequence: People want ordinary warmth, not a spotlight; just include them like anyone.

scenarios.debrief: Quiet, ordinary respect, like treating everyone the same, is understanding in action.
scenarios.relearn: Treat everyone with the same ordinary respect; quiet warmth beats a spotlight.

scenarios.hook: A friend insists 'everyone's basically the same, difference is made up'.

options.text: Gently say people really do vary, and that's the normal human thing
options.consequence: You replace a flat myth with a calm fact.

options.text: Agree to keep the peace
options.consequence: People genuinely vary; saying so kindly isn't picking a fight.

scenarios.debrief: Variety is the human norm; expecting everyone to be identical is the myth.
scenarios.relearn: People really do vary; that variety is the normal human thing.

scenarios.hook: You overhear a scary rumour about 'what those people are like'.

options.text: Don't pass it on; meet it with a calm fact instead
options.consequence: You stop fear and share understanding.

options.text: Repeat the rumour to others
options.consequence: Rumours spread fear; understanding replaces it with facts.

scenarios.debrief: Understanding replaces fear with facts; rumours just spread the fear.
scenarios.relearn: Don't pass on fear-based rumours; meet them with calm facts.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two moves here that cross a line into prying or labelling.

scene.text: Asking 'so what is she, really?' to gossip
Using the words people use for themselves
Reading someone's chats to guess about them
Listening when a friend shares
Letting people share at their own pace

scenarios.why: Gossip-guessing and snooping through chats are prying and labelling; the rest are respectful.
scenarios.relearn: Guessing for gossip and snooping cross the line; using people's own words, listening and patience don't.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two lines that are slurs or insults, not respectful words.

scene.text: A mocking nickname for someone
The word a person uses for themselves
An outdated, insulting label
A plain, neutral description
Just calling them by their name

scenarios.why: A mocking nickname and an outdated insult are slurs; people's own words, neutral terms and names are respectful.
scenarios.relearn: Mocking nicknames and outdated insults are slurs; people's own words, neutral terms and their names are respectful.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two myths hiding among these statements about the spectrum.

scene.text: "It's a brand-new fad"
People vary naturally in who they love
"It's a foreign import"
It spans cultures and history
It's part of India's own traditions

scenarios.why: 'A new fad' and 'a foreign import' are the myths; the rest are accurate facts.
scenarios.relearn: 'New fad' and 'foreign import' are myths; natural variation across history and India is fact.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two responses that wrongly turn understanding into labelling someone.

scene.text: "So you have to pick a label now?"
"Cool, thanks for telling me."
"Let me guess what you 'really' are."
"No rush. You don't owe me anything."
"We're the same as always."

scenarios.why: Pushing a label and guessing 'what you really are' force labelling; the others respect that understanding isn't labelling.
scenarios.relearn: Pushing a label or guessing is wrong; understanding never means labelling anyone.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two fear-based rumours mixed in with the calm facts.

scene.text: "Learning about it spreads it"
Understanding replaces fear with facts
"You can catch it from people"
People are simply who they are
Knowing the facts keeps people calmer

scenarios.why: 'It spreads' and 'you can catch it' are fear-based rumours; the rest are calm, accurate facts.
scenarios.relearn: 'It spreads' and 'you can catch it' are rumours; understanding replaces fear with facts.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two things here that are NOT how an ally acts.

scene.text: Joining in when others mock someone
Standing up for someone's dignity
Spreading a rumour about someone
Including a person who's left out
Using respectful words

scenarios.why: Joining mockery and spreading rumours are not allyship; backing dignity, including people and respectful words are.
scenarios.relearn: Mocking and spreading rumours aren't allyship; an ally backs dignity, includes people and uses respectful words.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two replies that make sharing weird instead of warm.

scene.text: Acting shocked and going quiet
"Thanks for trusting me."
Telling other people right after
"Nothing changes between us."
Treating them exactly the same

scenarios.why: Acting shocked and telling others betray trust; warmth, reassurance and staying the same are the respectful response.
scenarios.relearn: Shock and telling others make it weird; warmth, reassurance and staying the same are right.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two demands that don't belong in respectful curiosity.

scene.text: "Explain yourself to me right now."
"Tell me if I ever get a word wrong."
"Prove to us who you really are."
"Only share what you want to."
"I'll just ask kindly if I'm unsure."

scenarios.why: Demanding an explanation and 'prove who you are' pressure people; the rest are gentle and respect their pace.
scenarios.relearn: Demanding explanations or proof crosses a line; respectful curiosity asks gently and lets people set the pace.
